code: # KEGG network: network <- readRDS(url("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/network.kegg.rds")) metabolites.annotation <- readRDS(url("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/met.kegg.db.rds")) # combined network (KEGG+Rhea+transport reactions): network <- readRDS(url("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/network.combined.rds")) metabolites.annotation <- readRDS(url("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/met.combined.db.rds")) gene2reaction.extra <- data.table::fread("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/gene2reaction.combined.mmu.eg.tsv", colClasses="character") network.annotation <- readRDS(url("http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/publications/supp_materials/GATOM/org.Mm.eg.gatom.anno.rds")) met.to.filter <- data.table::fread(system.file("mets2mask.lst", package="GAMclust"))$ID solver <- mwcsr::rnc_solver() cplex.dir <-  "/opt/ibm/ILOG/CPLEX_Studio1271" solver <- mwcsr::virgo_solver(cplex_dir = cplex.dir) work.dir <- "results" dir.create(work.dir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T) stats.dir <- file.path(work.dir, "stats") dir.create(stats.dir, showWarnings = F, recursive = T)  setup_logger <- function(log.file.path, logger.name = "stats.logger") {   file.appender <- appender.file(log.file.path)   console.appender <- appender.console()   combined.appender <- function(line) {     file.appender(line)     console.appender(line)   }   flog.appender(combined.appender, name = logger.name)   flog.threshold(TRACE, name = logger.name) }  log.file <- file.path(stats.dir, "log.txt") setup_logger(log.file.path = log.file, logger.name = "stats.logger")

title: GAM-clustering Tutorial Notebook For Reanalysis Of [ImmGen Open Source](http://artyomovlab.wustl.edu/immgen-met/) Bulk RNA-Seq Data
text: Now everything prepared GAM-clustering analysis. Initial patterns now refined iterative process. output gamClustering() function presents set specific subnetworks (also called metabolic modules) reflect metabolic variability within given transcriptional dataset. Note, may take long time derive metabolic modules gamClustering() function (tens minutes). set parameters determine size number final modules. recommend start default settings, however can adjust based preferences: consider final modules small big complicates interpretation , can either increase reduce 10 units max.module.size parameter. among final modules consider presence modules similar patterns, can reduce 0.1 units cor.threshold parameter. among final modules consider presence uninformative modules, can reduce 10 times p.adj.val.threshold parameter.

title: GAM-clustering: Metabolic Modules Derivig From RNAseq Data
text: GAMclust R package identifying transcriptionally regulated metabolic modules complex RNA sequencing datasets. GAMclust implements flexible data processing pipeline designed analyze three major types RNA-seq data: bulk, single-cell, spatial. pipeline takes input gene expression matrix global metabolic network. initial preprocessing, inputs integrated GAM-clustering algorithm, identifies metabolic subnetworks (modules) correlated gene expression behaviors. aid interpretation results, several post-processing procedures carried , including visualization annotation modules. Interactive results GAM-clustering analysis ImmGen Open Source Tabula Muris data can explored , details Gainullina et al, 2023.

title: GAM-clustering analysis — gamClustering
text: Performs core GAM-clustering procedure identify transcriptionally coordinated metabolic modules. Starting initial expression patterns, algorithm iteratively scores genes, solves SGMWCS optimization problems metabolic network, updates module-specific expression profiles convergence. Additional refinement steps merge highly similar modules, remove uninformative patterns, control module size. function returns final metabolic modules, scored networks, module expression patterns, detailed iteration statistics.
